newsitem.title: UK: Expectations of Denmark in EMU rises - JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: Expectations of Denmark in EMU rises - JP Morgan.

text.p: Market expectations of Denmark taking part in European Monetary Union rose sharply over the past week, while the probability of the UK and Sweden participating receded, JP Morgan's EMU calculator showed.
The U.S. investment house's method of calculating market expectations of EMU taking place monitors bond yield spreads in the swaps market between participating European countries.

The latest calculation shows the probability of Denmark joining a single currency rose by 13.0 percentage points to 57 percent the five trading days to Friday, bringing its rise in just two weeks to more than 20 percentage points.

Italy too added to last week's gains and the probability assigned by financial markets to the lira being part of a single currency rose a further 4.0 percentage points to 56 percent, the JP Morgan index showed.
The UK recorded the biggest decline in EMU expectations for the second week running, sliding 10.0 points to 30 percent in the latest five day period. Sweden's rating dropped 7.0 points to 55 percent.
Elsewhere, Spain rose one point to 50.0 percent.
According to these calculations the market believes there is a 100 percent chance of France and Belgium being in EMU.

The calculator works by assigning a market probability level to each country. This is derived from the actual swap spread, an in-house assumption of what the spread would be if EMU were not a factor and the expected spread after EMU participation, which is zero.
